title: Fourier coefficients recover polynomial coefficients
statement: For any natural number $n$, any real coefficient family $p$ indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and every subset $S$ of that coordinate set, the Fourier--Walsh coefficient at $S$ of the polynomial represented by $p$ equals $p(S)$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of the coordinate set
$S$ is a subset of the coordinate set
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. For every $S\subseteq[n]$, $\widehat P(S)=a_S$.
